passenger-train.definition: A train used to transport people rather than freight.
passenger-train.exampleUsage: The passenger train carried travelers between the two cities.

freight-train.definition: A train used mainly to transport goods rather than passengers.
freight-train.exampleUsage: The freight train carried containers through the yard.

high-speed-train.definition: A passenger train designed to travel at very high speeds on suitable rail lines.
high-speed-train.exampleUsage: The high-speed train connects the cities on a suitable rail line.

subway.definition: An urban rapid-transit railway system, often partly or largely underground.
subway.exampleUsage: The subway provides rapid transit across the city.

locomotive.definition: A railway engine that pulls or pushes train cars.
locomotive.exampleUsage: The locomotive pulled the carriages from the station.

train-car.definition: One vehicle or carriage forming part of a train.
train-car.exampleUsage: Passengers entered the second train car.

dining-car.definition: A railway carriage that provides meals and drinks to passengers during a journey.
dining-car.exampleUsage: The dining car served meals during the journey.

sleeper-car.definition: A passenger train car containing beds or sleeping compartments for overnight travel.
sleeper-car.exampleUsage: The overnight train includes a sleeper car.

caboose.definition: A car on a freight train for use of the train crew.
caboose.arabicTranslation: عربة طاقم في مؤخرة قطار بضائع
caboose.exampleUsage: The historical freight train had a caboose for its crew.

monorail.definition: A railway system in which trains run on a single rail.
monorail.exampleUsage: The monorail runs on a single rail.

platform.definition: The area beside a railway track where passengers board or leave trains.
platform.exampleUsage: Passengers waited in the permitted area of the platform.

track.definition: The rails and supporting structure on which a train runs.
track.exampleUsage: Staff kept visitors away from the operating track.

ticket-office.definition: A staffed office where passengers buy train tickets.
ticket-office.exampleUsage: The traveler bought a ticket at the ticket office.

waiting-room.definition: A room where passengers sit while waiting for a train.
waiting-room.exampleUsage: Travelers rested in the waiting room.

concourse.definition: A large open area in a station through which passengers move.
concourse.exampleUsage: The traveler crossed the concourse toward the departure area.

information-desk.definition: A staffed service point helps visitors in public or institutional buildings find their way, ask questions, and obtain general assistance.
information-desk.exampleUsage: Staff at the information desk explained the current platform information.

newsstand.definition: A small shop or stand that sells newspapers and magazines.
newsstand.exampleUsage: The newsstand sells newspapers and magazines.

vending-machine.definition: A machine that dispenses products after a customer inserts payment.
vending-machine.exampleUsage: The vending machine dispensed a drink after payment.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.
restroom.exampleUsage: The traveler asked where the restroom was.

parking-garage.definition: A building or covered structure with multiple vehicle-parking spaces.
parking-garage.exampleUsage: The parking garage is connected to the station by a walkway.

taxi-stand.definition: A designated place where taxis wait to pick up passengers.
taxi-stand.exampleUsage: Passengers queued at the taxi stand.

bus-stop.definition: A designated roadside location where buses collect passengers or let them off, often identified by a sign, shelter, or raised platform.
bus-stop.exampleUsage: The bus stop is outside the station entrance.

ticket.definition: A printed or electronic document that permits travel on a train.
ticket.exampleUsage: The traveler showed the ticket to the conductor.

round-trip.definition: A journey that carries someone to a destination and back to the place of departure, or the combined distance or fare for both legs.
round-trip.exampleUsage: The fare covered a round trip between the cities.

one-way.definition: Describing a journey or ticket to a destination without a return journey.
one-way.exampleUsage: The traveler bought a one-way ticket without a return journey.

schedule.definition: A plan showing when events or activities will happen.
schedule.exampleUsage: The schedule lists the planned service times.

timetable.definition: A schedule listing events and the times at which they will take place.
timetable.exampleUsage: The timetable shows the train's scheduled departure.

departure-board.definition: A display showing scheduled departures, destinations, platforms, and times.
departure-board.exampleUsage: The departure board showed the current platform.

arrival-board.definition: A display showing incoming services, arrival times, and related information.
arrival-board.exampleUsage: The arrival board listed the delayed incoming train.

reservation.definition: Something reserved in advance (as a hotel accommodation or a seat on a plane etc.).
reservation.exampleUsage: The traveler made a reservation for a seat.

seat-number.definition: A number used to identify a specific passenger seat.
seat-number.exampleUsage: The ticket gives the booked seat number.

first-class.definition: A higher service class on some trains, usually offering different seating or amenities from standard class.
first-class.exampleUsage: The traveler compared first class with the operator's other service categories.

economy-class.definition: A travel section on a ship, train, or plane that costs less than first class.
economy-class.exampleUsage: The booking was for economy class under the operator's service terms.

pass.definition: A ticket that permits specified train journeys over a period of time.
pass.exampleUsage: The pass allows specified journeys during its validity period.

turnstile.definition: A gate consisting of a post that acts as a pivot for rotating arms.
turnstile.exampleUsage: The turnstile rotated to admit the passenger.

signal.definition: A railway light or sign that tells train drivers when to stop or proceed.
signal.exampleUsage: The signal displayed information for the train driver.

crossing-gate.definition: A movable barrier that blocks road or pedestrian traffic when a train is approaching a railway crossing.
crossing-gate.exampleUsage: The crossing gate lowered before the train passed.

bridge.definition: A structure that carries a railway or road over water, a valley, or another route.
bridge.exampleUsage: The railway bridge crosses the river.

tunnel.definition: An enclosed passage through or beneath land or another structure.
tunnel.exampleUsage: The train traveled through a tunnel beneath the hill.

overhead-wire.definition: An electrical wire suspended above a railway line to supply power to electric trains.
overhead-wire.exampleUsage: The compatible electric train draws power from an overhead wire.

rail.definition: A metal track on which a train runs.
rail.exampleUsage: The wheel runs along the metal rail.

switch.definition: A movable section of railway track that guides a train onto another track.
switch.exampleUsage: The switch guides the train onto a different track.

buffer-stop.definition: A structure installed at the end of a railway track to limit movement beyond it under specified design conditions.
buffer-stop.exampleUsage: The buffer stop stands at the end of the track.

clock-tower.definition: A tower designed with a large clock displayed high on an exterior wall.
clock-tower.exampleUsage: The clock tower shows the time above the station entrance.

conductor.definition: A train crew member who checks tickets and assists passengers.
conductor.exampleUsage: The conductor checked the passengers' tickets.

engineer.definition: The person who operates a locomotive; also called a train driver.
engineer.exampleUsage: The engineer operated the locomotive in this US rail account.

porter.definition: A worker who helps passengers carry luggage.
porter.exampleUsage: The porter helped the traveler carry luggage.

commuter.definition: A person who regularly travels between home and work or study.
commuter.exampleUsage: The commuter travels between home and work regularly.

traveler.exampleUsage: The traveler asked about the onward connection.

boarding.exampleUsage: Boarding began after the staff announcement.

departing.definition: Leaving a place or beginning the outward journey.
departing.exampleUsage: The train is departing from the station.

arriving.definition: Getting to a place or the end of a trip.
arriving.exampleUsage: The train is arriving at its destination.

transferring.definition: Changing from one train or transport service to another.
transferring.exampleUsage: The traveler is transferring to another service.

waiting.definition: The act of waiting (remaining inactive in one place while expecting something).
waiting.exampleUsage: The passengers are waiting for the next train.

announcing.definition: Giving passengers spoken information, such as a departure time.
announcing.exampleUsage: The staff member is announcing the platform change.

validating.definition: Checking or marking a ticket to confirm that it can be used.
validating.exampleUsage: The operator requires validating the ticket before the stated journey.
